```{r}
  "clustering-k_clusters",            "Number of clusters (k-means)",       "6",
  "clustering-dist_function",         "Distance measure",                   "1",
  "pca-encircle",                     "Encircle groups",                    "0",
  "deg-limma_p_val",                  "FDR cutoff",                         "0.1",
  "deg-limma_fc",                     "Min. fold-change",                   "2",
  "deg-plot_color_select_1",          "Plot colors",                        "Green-Red",
  "deg-plot_color_select",            "Plot colors",                        "Green-Red",
  "deg-gene_direction_filter",        "Gene direction",                     "Up-regulated genes",
  "deg-label_volcano-num_genes",      "Volcano plot: label top n genes",    "5",
  "pathway-pathway_method",           "Pathway analysis method",            "3",
  "pathway-pathway_p_val_cutoff",     "Pathway significance cutoff (FDR)",  "0.1",
  "pathway-pgsea_plot_color_select",  "PGSEA plot colors",                  "Blue-Red",
  "pathway-kegg_color_select",        "KEGG colors (low-high)",             "Green-Red"
)

# Settings whose logged value is a code, with the label shown in the app
choice_labels <- tribble(
  ~id,                              ~value,              ~label,
  "pre_process-counts_transform",   "1",                 "edgeR: log-CPM",
  "pre_process-counts_transform",   "2",                 "VST",
  "pre_process-counts_transform",   "3",                 "rlog",
  "pre_process-missing_value",      "geneMedian",        "Use gene median",
  "pre_process-missing_value",      "treatAsZero",       "Treat as zero",
  "pre_process-missing_value",      "geneMedianInGroup", "Use gene median in group",
  "clustering-cluster_meth",        "1",                 "Hierarchical",
  "clustering-cluster_meth",        "2",                 "k-Means",
  "clustering-dendrogram_display",  "row",               "Row",
  "clustering-dendrogram_display",  "column",            "Column",
  "clustering-dendrogram_display",  "both",              "Both",
  "clustering-dendrogram_display",  "none",              "None",
  "clustering-dist_function",       "1",                 "Pearson",
  "clustering-dist_function",       "2",                 "Euclidean",
  "clustering-dist_function",       "3",                 "Absolute Pearson",
  "pca-encircle",                   "0",                 "Off",
  "pca-encircle",                   "1",                 "On",
  "pathway-pathway_method",         "1",                 "GAGE",
  "pathway-pathway_method",         "2",                 "PGSEA",
  "pathway-pathway_method",         "3",                 "GSEA (preranked fgsea)",
  "pathway-pathway_method",         "4",                 "PGSEA w/ all samples",
  "pathway-pathway_method",         "5",                 "ReactomePA",
  "pathway-pathway_method",         "6",                 "GSVA",
  "pathway-pathway_method",         "7",                 "ssGSEA",
  "pathway-pathway_method",         "8",                 "PLAGE"
)
choice_label <- \(id, value) {
  coalesce(choice_labels$label[match(paste(id, value), paste(choice_labels$id, choice_labels$value))],
           value)
}

# Each session's last value of each setting. Numbers are compared as
# numbers, so 0.10 counts as the default 0.1.
last_values <- events |>
  filter(session %in% loaded_sessions, type == "input", user_action,
         id %in% settings$id, !is.na(value)) |>
  group_by(id, session) |>
  slice_max(time, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  inner_join(settings, by = "id") |>
  mutate(
    num_value   = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(value)),
    num_default = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(default)),
    changed     = if_else(!is.na(num_value) & !is.na(num_default),
                          num_value != num_default, value != default)
  )

# Sessions that used each tab (over 5 seconds), as the denominator
tab_users <- count(distinct(used_visits, session, tab), tab, name = "tab_sessions")

# The most common value among sessions that changed each setting
top_new <- last_values |>
  filter(changed) |>
  count(id, value, name = "n_new") |>
  group_by(id) |>
  slice_max(n_new, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()

settings_changed <- last_values |>
  group_by(id, setting, default) |>
  summarise(tab = names(which.max(table(tab))), sessions = sum(changed), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(tab_users, by = "tab") |>
  left_join(top_new, by = "id") |>
  mutate(
    pct         = 100 * sessions / tab_sessions,
    default_lbl = choice_label(id, default),
    new_lbl     = if_else(is.na(value), "", paste0(choice_label(id, value), " (", num(n_new), ")"))
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(sessions))

knitr::kable(
  select(settings_changed, setting, tab, default_lbl, sessions, pct, new_lbl),
  col.names = c("Setting", "Tab", "Default", "Sessions that changed it",
                "% of sessions that used the tab", "Most common new value (sessions)"),
  digits = 1,
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  caption = "Settings with a fixed default, by the number of sessions that ended on a different value"
)
```

```{r}
#| label: findings-settings
#| include: false

by_share <- arrange(settings_changed, desc(pct))
setting_row <- \(i) filter(settings_changed, id == i)
fdr <- setting_row("deg-limma_p_val")
fc  <- setting_row("deg-limma_fc")
top_color <- filter(by_share, grepl("colors", setting))[1, ]
```

- By number of sessions, the most changed settings are `r knitr::combine_words(paste0(head(settings_changed$setting, 3), " on ", head(settings_changed$tab, 3), " (", num(head(settings_changed$sessions, 3)), ")"))`. As a share of the sessions that used the tab, the top ones are `r knitr::combine_words(paste0(head(by_share$setting, 3), " on ", head(by_share$tab, 3), " (", pct(head(by_share$pct, 3)), ")"))`.
- On Stats, `r pct(fdr$pct)` of the analysis sessions that used the tab changed the FDR cutoff from `r fdr$default_lbl`, most often to `r fdr$value` (`r num(fdr$n_new)` sessions), and `r pct(fc$pct)` changed the minimum fold-change from `r fc$default_lbl`, most often to `r fc$value` (`r num(fc$n_new)`).
- Color settings are rarely changed: even the most often changed one, `r top_color$setting` on `r top_color$tab`, was changed in only `r pct(top_color$pct)` of the sessions that used the tab.

:::

## Summary

<!-- This tab comes last so it can use numbers from every section above;
     the script at the end makes the page open on it. -->

### Who's counted

The report counts **sessions**: one visit to iDEP, from opening the app to closing it. Each finding is out of one of these groups, and says which.

**A session is not a person.** The telemetry gives every session a new anonymous ID, so sessions from the same person can't be linked. One person can show up as several sessions: loading new data or pressing Reset starts a new session, and so does coming back another day. The report can't say how many people use iDEP, only how many sessions.

```{r}
#| label: whos-counted
#| echo: false

tibble(
  Group = c("All sessions", "Active sessions", "Analysis sessions",
            "Successful sessions", paste("Sessions since", day_label(last_generic))),
  Sessions = num(c(n_sessions_all, n_distinct(events$session), length(loaded_sessions),
                   nrow(successful), length(recent_sessions))),
  Definition = c(
    paste0("Every session logged, ", day_label(min(events$time)), " to ",
           day_label(max(events$time)), "."),
    "Sessions that did at least one thing (a click, upload or setting change). The rest did nothing and are left out of the whole report.",
    "Active sessions that loaded data, their own or a demo.",
    "Analysis sessions that downloaded at least one thing.",
    "Active sessions that started after every error began to record what went wrong."
  ),
  "Used in" = c(
    "Totals only",
    "Time of day, Session length, Errors",
    "How users use iDEP, Analysis paths, Own data vs. demo, settings in Where iDEP falls short",
    "Successful sessions, Analysis paths",
    "Problems in Where iDEP falls short"
  )
) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrll")
```

### Key findings

```{r}
#| label: summary-findings
#| include: false

# The three problems that affected the most sessions since the logging
# change, with the tab where most of them happened
top3_problems <- head(problems, 3) |>
  mutate(main_tab = sub(" \\(.*", "", where))
stats_gap <- filter(tab_gap, tab == "Stats")
```

- **Who uses iDEP.** `r num(n_sessions_all)` sessions over about `r n_days` days. `r pct(100 * length(idle_sessions) / n_sessions_all)` did nothing, and `r pct(100 * length(loaded_sessions) / n_sessions_all)` loaded data (analysis sessions). Use peaks overnight in US Central time: `r pct(overnight)` of active sessions fall between 8 p.m. and 5 a.m. (*Time of day*, *How users use iDEP*)
- **Success.** `r pct(100 * nrow(successful) / length(loaded_sessions))` of analysis sessions download at least one result. Successful sessions get to the comparison results: `r pct(stats_gap$Successful)` of them used Stats, compared with `r pct(stats_gap$"No download")` of analysis sessions with no download. (*How users use iDEP*)
- **Where users stop.** `r pct(only_data)` of analysis sessions never get past Data, and half of those leave within `r mins(median(stuck$after_load))` of loading their data. `r share(stuck$groups == "1")` of them have only one sample group, so there's nothing to compare. (*How users use iDEP*)
- **Crashes come from uploaded files.** Since `r day_label(last_generic)`, `r num(upload_crashes)` of the `r num(n_distinct(recent_fatal$session))` sessions that crashed did so right after a file upload, and `r share(demo$crashed)` of demo sessions crashed. (*Where iDEP falls short*, *Own data vs. demo*)
- **A few bugs cause most errors.** `r pct(100 * recent_error_sessions / length(recent_sessions))` of sessions since `r day_label(last_generic)` hit an error, and the 10 most common problems account for `r pct(100 * top10_sessions / recent_error_sessions)` of them. The biggest are `r knitr::combine_words(paste0('"', esc(top3_problems$problem), '" on ', top3_problems$main_tab, " (", num(top3_problems$sessions), " sessions)"))`. (*Where iDEP falls short*)
- **Two Stats defaults may be wrong.** `r pct(fdr$pct)` of analysis sessions that used Stats changed the FDR cutoff from `r fdr$default_lbl` (most often to `r fdr$value`), and `r pct(fc$pct)` changed the minimum fold-change from `r fc$default_lbl` (most often to `r fc$value`). (*Where iDEP falls short*)
- **Demo users look; own-data users take results away.** `r share(demo$downloads > 0)` of demo sessions downloaded anything, compared with `r share(own$downloads > 0)` of own-data sessions, and `r report_pct("Demo data")` of demo users' downloads are reports, compared with `r report_pct("Own data")` for own-data users. (*Own data vs. demo*)
